text:
An approval screen is no place to stop checking.

CERT-In reports an AI-assisted campaign targeting Indian financial entities through their payment interfaces. Its earlier advisory describes stolen credentials enabling direct payment calls that bypass application checks.

That’s the gap I’d want leaders to examine: a screen can show approval without proving that the system moving the money requires it.

The distinction matters. If the transfer can happen without checking the approved decision, confidence in the screen tells you little about control over the payment.

My recommendation: ask the business owner and IT lead to trace one approved payment all the way to transfer. Match the recipient and amount. Identify what permission the final transfer accepts, and what would stop it if those details changed after approval.

One trace won’t establish that every payment is protected. But it gives leaders something concrete to assess beyond a reassuring display.

The evidence worth asking for sits where money actually moves.
